title: Documents: engagement letters, e-sign, matter files, templates, AI drafting, review, precedents
summary: Each matter has one document store. The agent files, names, OCRs and indexes everything that arrives, and drafts outgoing documents from templates, precedents and matter facts. Every factual claim in a draft carries a page/line citation back to a source document. Nothing leaves the firm until a named lawyer approves it: G5 for the engagement letter, G8 for any other outgoing document. The client signs the engagement letter through our own e-sign flow, with a full audit trail.

screens.name: Engagement letter composer
screens.purpose: Turn intake and conflict output into an engagement or retainer letter that the lawyer approves before it is sent for signature.
screens.layout: Left: the letter, editable, with highlighted variable terms. Right: a terms panel (scope, fee basis, rates, retainer, HST, exclusions) and a compliance checklist. Top bar: status, approver, Send for signature.

fields.name: letter_type
fields.note: full-scope | limited-scope | contingency (LSO standard form) | non-engagement | disengagement

fields.name: client
fields.note: Contact(s) who sign. Joint clients need a joint-retainer clause.

fields.name: scope_included
fields.note: What we will do, in plain language

fields.name: scope_excluded
fields.note: Required for limited scope

fields.name: fee_basis
fields.note: hourly | flat | blended | contingency

fields.name: rates
fields.note: Per timekeeper, from the rate table

fields.name: retainer_amount
fields.note: Deposited to trust, never to operating

fields.name: hst_applies

actions.name: Draft letter
actions.note: Built from the intake summary, the conflict result and the matter-type default template

actions.name: Edit terms
actions.note: A term edit regenerates the affected clauses only

actions.name: Approve letter
actions.note: G5. Only the responsible lawyer can approve. Approval locks the text and hashes it.

actions.name: Send for signature
actions.note: Allowed only after G5. Opens a signature request.

actions.name: Revoke and redraft
actions.note: Voids any open signature request

screens.agent: Picks the template by matter type and fee basis. Fills scope from the intake facts. Pulls rates from the rate table. Adds a limited-scope clause and an exclusions list when needed. Switches to the LSO standard form for contingency matters. Runs the checklist: scope stated, fee basis, retainer to trust, HST, termination, file retention, joint-retainer disclosure. Each check shows pass or fail with its reason.
screens.gate: G5: the responsible lawyer approves the exact letter text (scope, fees, retainer, estimate). The approved version is hashed, and the signed copy must match that hash.
edge: Conflict not cleared: Approve is disabled and the screen links to the conflict check
Contingency fee: the free-form template is blocked. Only the LSO standard form, with fields filled in, is allowed.
Joint clients with possibly divergent interests: a joint-retainer warning appears, plus a separate consent block
Text edited after approval: the approval is cleared and G5 has to be redone
The client asks for changes after sending: void the request, redraft, re-approve
screens.reg: RPC 3.6-1 requires fees to be fair, reasonable and disclosed in a timely way. RPC 3.2-1A on limited-scope retainers: the scope should be confirmed in writing (verify). RPC 3.4 joint retainers need disclosure and consent. Contingency fees: O. Reg. 563/20 under the Solicitors Act requires the LSO 'Standard Form Contingency Fee Agreement' dated Nov 18, 2021, modified only by filling in matter details or choosing its options (verify current version). A non-compliant agreement risks being found void.

rows: No assumptions listed for the $3,000 to $4,500 range

screens.name: Signature request tracker
screens.purpose: Track an outgoing signature package from send to completion, with signer order, reminders and a tamper-evident audit trail.
screens.layout: Header: package status and document hash. Middle: a signer list with order, status, last activity and identity method. Bottom: an audit timeline. Side: the signed PDF and certificate once complete.

fields.name: signers

fields.name: identity_method

fields.name: signing_fields
fields.note: Signature, initials, date, text; placed by the agent and adjustable

fields.name: expires_at
fields.note: Default 14 days (owner choice). Clio is inconsistent: its intake product says 7 days in one place and 14 in another.

fields.name: reminder_plan
fields.note: None | days 3 and 7 (default) | every 3 days | custom

fields.name: witness_required
fields.note: Set by template, for example on contingency agreements (verify under current form)

fields.name: signing_order
fields.note: parallel | sequential with order

fields.name: field_types
fields.note: signature, initials, date signed, text, checkbox, dropdown, radio; fields can show based on another field

fields.name: firm_presign
fields.note: Lawyer signs before client

fields.name: non_contact_signer
fields.note: Ad-hoc signer allowed; created as a contact with role 'signer'

fields.name: viewed_at
fields.note: Firm notified when opened

actions.name: Place signing fields
actions.note: Uses the template's anchors, or detected signature blocks

actions.name: Send
actions.note: Only approved versions can be sent

actions.name: Remind
actions.note: Follows the reminder plan, using an approved reminder template

actions.name: Void
actions.note: Requires a reason, which goes to audit

actions.name: Countersign
actions.note: The lawyer signs last, where the template needs it

actions.name: File completed copy
actions.note: Saves the signed PDF plus certificate to the matter folder and advances the matter stage

screens.agent: Sends reminders on schedule. Spots a bounced email or a stalled signer and tells the clerk. Once complete, checks that the signed document's hash matches the approved version. Files the signed copy and certificate, sends the client their copy, and fires the 'engagement signed' event, which triggers the trust retainer request.
screens.gate: None to send, since the document already passed G5 or G8. The lawyer's countersignature is a sign-off where the document needs one.
edge: A signer declines with a comment: the comment goes to the lawyer and the letter returns to draft
Wrong email address: void, fix the contact, resend. The old link is dead.
Hash mismatch on completion: block filing and alert the lawyer
Document type excluded from e-signature (will, power of attorney): Send is blocked and the screen offers a wet-ink signing checklist instead
Signer is a corporation: capture the signing officer's name and title, and 'I have authority to bind the corporation'
Link expires (default 14 days): signer can ask for a fresh link; firm sees 'expired'
Non-PDF upload: converted to PDF and the converted copy is what is signed
screens.reg: Electronic Commerce Act, 2000 (Ontario): electronic signatures are generally valid. Section 31 excludes wills, codicils, trusts created by wills, and powers of attorney for property or personal care (verify current text). Keep the audit trail with the file. Signer identity ties into BL 7.1 client ID where funds will move.

screens.name: Client signing page
screens.purpose: Let the client read, ask a question about, and sign a document on any device without creating an account.
screens.layout: Top: firm name and a step indicator (verify, review, sign). Centre: the document, with signing fields highlighted. Bottom: Sign, Decline, and Ask the lawyer a question.

fields.name: verification_code
fields.note: SMS or email code when the identity method needs one

fields.name: consent_to_electronic
fields.note: An explicit checkbox agreeing to sign electronically

fields.name: signature
fields.note: Typed name or drawn

actions.name: Ask a question
actions.note: Goes to the lawyer's inbox. The agent does not answer substantive questions on this page.

actions.name: Download copy
actions.note: Available after completion

screens.agent: None on this page. It records audit events (opened, viewed each page, signed, IP address, device). It does not chat with the client here, so it cannot give unapproved advice.
edge: Link forwarded to someone else: the second factor (SMS) blocks them
Screen reader or low vision: must meet WCAG 2.1 AA; AODA applies in Ontario (verify which tier)
Client wants French: show the French template version where the firm offers one
screens.reg: Confidentiality (RPC 3.3): links expire and are single-purpose. Accessibility (AODA, verify). Data stays in Canada.

screens.name: Matter documents
screens.purpose: Show one place for every document on a matter, with folders, filing status, privilege flags and quick actions.
screens.layout: Left: a folder tree, seeded from the matter-type folder template. Centre: the document table. Right: a filing queue of items the agent filed with low confidence or flagged as privileged.

fields.name: title

fields.name: doc_type
fields.note: pleading | correspondence | agreement | evidence | ID | financial | court order | internal note | ...

fields.name: source
fields.note: upload | email | portal | generated | scanned

fields.name: privilege

fields.name: ocr_status
fields.note: n/a | queued | done | low quality

fields.name: client_visible
fields.note: Shared to the portal. Off by default.

fields.name: retention_class
fields.note: Inherited from the matter, and drives the destruction date

fields.name: doc_category
fields.note: From document settings

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft | in review | final | sent | signed. Set by the agent from events (review approved, sent, signature completed); a person can correct it.

fields.name: classification
fields.note: Legal type proposed by the agent (for example statement of claim, affidavit, lease). Distinct from doc_type, which is the broad group.

fields.name: tags
fields.note: Up to 10 free tags per document

fields.name: received_at
fields.note: Date the firm received the document, not the upload time. The agent reads it from a stamp, the email header or a service note. Feeds limitation and service deadlines through G7.

fields.name: locked_by
fields.note: User or agent job holding the edit lock

actions.name: Upload / drop / email-in
actions.note: Each matter has its own email-in address

actions.name: Auto-file
actions.note: Names, classifies, OCRs and files the document. Queued for review when confidence is low.

actions.name: Confirm filing
actions.note: G-D1. Only for low-confidence items or privilege flags.

actions.name: Share to client portal
actions.note: A privileged or internal document can never be shared without a warning acknowledgement

actions.name: Move / rename / delete
actions.note: Deletion is soft and goes to audit. A legal hold blocks it.

actions.name: New from template
actions.note: Opens document assembly

actions.name: Bulk download (zip)
actions.note: Lawyer for full-matter export; logged

actions.name: Lock / unlock
actions.note: Unlock by the person who locked it or a lawyer on the matter. The agent locks a document while it drafts a new version and releases it on save.

actions.name: Branch as new version
actions.note: Offered when someone edits a locked document; the edit becomes a separate version instead of overwriting.

screens.agent: Files each incoming document to the right folder. Proposes a name and a type. Runs OCR and extracts key data (dates, parties, amounts, deadlines), and sends deadlines to the calendar for G7. Flags privileged items and duplicates. Keeps the matter brief up to date.
screens.gate: G-D1: a clerk or lawyer confirms filing only when the agent is unsure (confidence below threshold), the item is flagged privileged, or it looks like it belongs to another matter.
edge: Email attachment matches two matters: queue it and never guess
Possible misdirected document from opposing counsel (privileged): quarantine it, alert the lawyer, and do not open it further (RPC 7.2-10, verify)
Password-protected or corrupt file: store as is and flag it
Very large scans (500+ pages): OCR runs in the background with progress shown
Duplicate upload: link it as the same document, with no new version
Lock held by a user who has left or is away: a lawyer on the matter can break the lock; the break is logged and the holder is told
received_at the agent could not read with confidence: left blank and flagged; no deadline is computed from a guessed date
screens.reg: Confidentiality (RPC 3.3) and privilege. Retention and destruction follow LSO file-management guidance (verify periods). Client ID copies follow BL 7.1 retention (verify period). All storage stays in the firm's Canadian cell.

screens.name: Document viewer
screens.purpose: Read a document (PDF, Word or image) with a searchable OCR text layer, page/line anchors, versions, comments and extracted data.
screens.layout: Centre: a page viewer with zoom, thumbnails and line numbers. Right tabs: Details, Extracted, Versions, Comments, Activity. Top: search in document, download, Ask about this document.

fields.name: text_layer
fields.note: Native text or OCR, with line positions kept so citations can point to page:line

fields.name: ocr_confidence
fields.note: Per page. Low pages are shaded.

fields.name: extracted
fields.note: Dates, parties, amounts, obligations, each with page:line

fields.name: versions
fields.note: Author, time, hash, change summary

fields.name: comments
fields.note: Anchored to a text range. Internal only.

fields.name: history
fields.note: History tab: uploads, versions, views, shares, signature events, and every agent read (which job read it, when, and for what purpose)

fields.name: source_highlight
fields.note: When opened from any review card (filing, deadline, intake fact, conflict hit, draft citation), the page scrolls to the cited span and highlights it beside the extracted value

actions.name: Search in document
actions.note: Covers the OCR text too

actions.name: Ask about this document
actions.note: The agent answers with page:line citations, and clicking one jumps to the highlight

actions.name: Compare versions
actions.note: A redline between any two versions

actions.name: Restore version
actions.note: Creates a new version. History is never rewritten.

actions.name: Re-run OCR
actions.note: Uses a higher-quality pass

actions.name: Accept extracted deadline
actions.note: Hands off to G7 in the calendar area

actions.name: Show history
actions.note: Filter by person, agent job or event type; export is logged

screens.agent: Builds the text layer and line map. Summarizes the document. Extracts data with citations. Proposes deadlines and tasks. Answers questions about this document only, citing page and line.
screens.gate: None to view. Extracted deadlines go to G7 (calendar area).
edge: Handwriting or a poor scan: mark the low-confidence lines. Citations to them show a 'verify against image' badge.
Rotated or mixed-size pages: line numbers are computed per rendered page
A Word document has no fixed pages: cite against a frozen PDF rendering of that version
Viewing a superseded version: a banner links to the current one
An agent read of a privilege-flagged document still in the G-D1 queue must never happen; if one is logged it raises an incident
screens.reg: Privilege labels are shown on every page and on downloads. Downloads are watermarked with user and time when the document is marked confidential.

screens.name: Document search
screens.purpose: Search across a matter or across all matters the user can access, by keyword, phrase or meaning, including OCR text.
screens.layout: Top: a query box with a matter scope picker and filters (type, date, party, privilege, folder). Results: snippets with the hit highlighted and a page:line reference. Side: an optional AI answer with citations.

fields.name: query
fields.note: Keyword, "exact phrase", or a natural-language question

fields.name: scope
fields.note: this matter | my matters | all accessible

fields.name: mode
fields.note: keyword | semantic | both

actions.name: Search
actions.note: Access is checked per matter. Hits on matters the user is walled off from are never shown or counted.

actions.name: Answer with citations
actions.note: Answers only from the hits, and says so when no hit supports an answer

screens.agent: Rewrites the query to cover synonyms. Ranks hits. Writes a short cited answer. Never pulls content from matters outside the user's access or behind an ethical wall.
edge: Ethical wall: walled matters are excluded at the index level, not hidden afterwards
OCR still running on new documents: show 'n documents not yet searchable'
Query names a client from a conflicted matter: no leakage through counts or suggestions
screens.reg: Confidentiality and conflicts screens (RPC 3.4 commentary on screening, verify) mean access control comes before ranking.

rows: ...rent shall abate in proportion to the area rendered unfit...
...the defendant failed to repair the brake line...

screens.name: Template library and editor
screens.purpose: Manage firm templates with merge fields, conditional clauses and optional clauses. Each template is versioned and approved before use.
screens.layout: List: templates by practice area and type, with status and owner. Editor: the document on the left, and a field/logic panel on the right (fields, conditions, clause picks), plus a test-fill preview using a sample matter.

fields.name: doc_kind
fields.note: engagement letter | letter | agreement | pleading | form | email

fields.name: fields
fields.note: Each field maps to a matter, contact or custom field, or is an ask-at-assembly question

fields.name: conditions
fields.note: If/else clause blocks, for example 'if limited scope'

fields.name: locked_text
fields.note: For example, the LSO contingency form: only fields and options can change

fields.name: language
fields.note: en | fr

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft | pending approval | published | retired

fields.name: source_format
fields.note: Word, fillable PDF, spreadsheet

fields.name: preview_matter
fields.note: Fill preview with a real matter's data

fields.name: court_forms
fields.note: Court forms tab: official Ontario forms first (Rules of Civil Procedure, Family Law Rules, estates), each with source URL, official version date and checksum

fields.name: built_on_form_version
fields.note: For firm templates built on a court form: the official version used

actions.name: Propose fields
actions.note: Finds blanks, sample names and dates in the imported file and proposes merge fields

actions.name: Test fill
actions.note: Runs against a sample matter. Unfilled fields are listed.

actions.name: Publish
actions.note: G-D2: a lawyer approves the template version. Matters pin the version they used.

actions.name: Retire
actions.note: Existing documents keep their pinned version

actions.name: Flag templates on old form versions
actions.note: A daily job compares official form versions; firm templates built on an old version are flagged and blocked from new assembly until a lawyer republishes (G-D2)

actions.name: Request a form
actions.note: Adds a form to the internal backlog

screens.agent: Converts an uploaded Word file into a template with proposed fields and conditions. Flags clauses that conflict with firm standards or are out of date (for example, an old contingency form date). Suggests where an approved precedent clause should replace free text.
screens.gate: G-D2: a lawyer approves each published template version, because every document generated from it inherits its text.
edge: A field mapped to a custom field that was later deleted: block publishing and list the broken fields
Regulator form updated (for example, the LSO standard form): the agent opens a change request and the old version stays published until replaced
Circular or contradictory conditions: the test fill fails with the path shown
One template cannot embed another: use clause blocks instead
Official form page unreachable or changed layout: keep the last known version, show 'unable to check since <date>' and do not auto-flag
screens.reg: The LSO contingency fee form must stay unmodified apart from its fillable fields and options (O. Reg. 563/20, verify). French-language services where offered.

screens.name: Document assembly
screens.purpose: Generate one document or a set from templates, prefilled with matter data. Only the missing answers are asked for.
screens.layout: Step 1: pick a template or document set. Step 2: a short questionnaire with only the missing fields, each prefilled answer showing where it came from. Step 3: a preview of every output, then Save as draft to the matter.

fields.name: template_or_set
fields.note: A set is an ordered list of templates, for example a closing package

fields.name: answers
fields.note: Each one is marked from matter | from document p:l | entered by user

fields.name: output_format
fields.note: docx | pdf

fields.name: which_client
fields.note: When a matter has several clients, pick whose data fills client fields

fields.name: output_both
fields.note: Word and PDF together

fields.name: case_facts
fields.note: Panel listing every field as resolved, missing, conflicting (two sources disagree, each cited) or role-unassigned. Generate is blocked until none are missing or conflicting.

fields.name: trigger
fields.note: manual | on matter open | on stage change (filters: practice area, responsible lawyer, from stage, to stage). Automatic runs land in target_folder and go to G8 before anything leaves the firm.

fields.name: client_questionnaire
fields.note: Questionnaire built only from unresolved fields; status not started | in progress | needs review | completed

actions.name: Prefill
actions.note: From matter fields, and from source documents with citations

actions.name: Generate
actions.note: Saved as a draft. Never sent.

actions.name: Send to review
actions.note: Hands off to the document review screen (G8)

actions.name: Regenerate set
actions.note: After matter data changes

actions.name: Resolve fact conflict
actions.note: Pick a source or type a value; the choice is cited and saved to matter facts

actions.name: Ask client for missing answers
actions.note: Agent builds the questionnaire and a portal link; a lawyer or clerk approves the wording before it is sent. Reviewed answers save to matter facts with source = client before Generate.

screens.agent: Prefills from the matter and its documents, citing where each value came from. Spots values that disagree, for example two different closing dates across documents, and asks instead of picking one. Generates the outputs and files them as drafts.
screens.gate: None here. The outputs are drafts and go to G8 before leaving the firm.
edge: Conflicting values across sources: they are shown side by side and a person must choose
Required field unknown: generation is blocked. A placeholder is never silently used.
Template version retired mid-flow: warn and offer the current version
Client answer contradicts an existing fact: it lands as a conflicting fact, never overwrites
Stage-change trigger fires twice (stage moved back and forth): the second run is skipped if an ungenerated or unreviewed set already exists
screens.reg: Competence (RPC 3.1): the lawyer stays responsible for the generated content.

rows: APS p.2 l.4 vs amendment p.1 l.6 (choose)

screens.name: AI drafting workspace
screens.purpose: Have the agent draft a letter, memo, pleading or agreement from matter sources and precedents. Every factual sentence is cited to a page:line in a source document.
screens.layout: Left: the draft, with citation chips inline. Right: the source pane, which opens the cited page with the lines highlighted. Top: the instruction, the precedents used, and a citation-coverage meter. Bottom: a chat to revise the draft.

fields.name: instruction
fields.note: For example: 'Demand letter to landlord re rent abatement, firm but courteous'

fields.name: sources
fields.note: Matter documents in scope. Defaults to all, and can be narrowed.

fields.name: precedents
fields.note: From the precedent library, chosen by the agent and editable

fields.name: citations
fields.note: claim span -> doc, version hash, page, line range, quote

fields.name: unsupported_claims
fields.note: Sentences that state a fact but have no citation

fields.name: legal_authorities
fields.note: Cases or statutes cited. Each one shows 'not verified' until a person checks it.

fields.name: revise_mode
fields.note: tracked | direct. Tracked is the default for any document that already exists or came from outside the firm.

fields.name: redlines
fields.note: Tracked mode: each change is an insert or delete with its reason and a citation; accept or reject per change or in bulk

actions.name: Revise by instruction
actions.note: Through the chat or inline comments

actions.name: Open citation
actions.note: Jumps to the exact lines

actions.name: Mark authority verified
actions.note: A person confirms the case or statute exists and says what the draft claims

actions.name: Send to review
actions.note: G8 review

actions.name: Accept / reject change
actions.note: Per change; unresolved changes block Send to review

screens.agent: Retrieves the relevant passages. Drafts in the precedent's structure and the firm's style. Attaches a page:line citation to each factual claim and quotes the source text in the chip. Marks any claim it cannot support. Never invents a case citation: it lists authorities as 'to verify' unless they come from a verified source.
screens.gate: None on this screen. 'Send to review' moves the draft to G8.
edge: A cited source document gets a new version: citations pinned to the old hash are flagged stale
A quote does not match the source text (OCR drift): the chip turns red and the sentence counts as unsupported
The instruction asks for something outside the matter's scope (limited retainer): warn
Sources include privileged internal notes and the output is going out of the firm: warn before citing them
Agent change with no reason or citation is shown as unsupported and cannot be bulk-accepted
screens.reg: LSO generative AI guidance (white paper and practice note, April 2024): the licensee remains responsible. Main risks: confidentiality, hallucination and accuracy, supervision. Competence (RPC 3.1). Some Ontario courts require disclosure or certification of AI use or authorities in filed documents (verify the current practice direction).

rows: Section 9.3 provides for rent abatement when premises are unfit.
The roof leak began on September 12.
Your client has acknowledged the defect.
See 1234 Holdings v. Example Corp, 2019 ONSC 0000.

screens.name: Document review (approval)
screens.purpose: Show the lawyer's queue of outgoing documents waiting for approval (G8), with the agent's pre-checks, a redline against the precedent, and a citation audit.
screens.layout: Queue list on the left (matter, document, due, risk). Centre: the document, toggling between clean view and redline against the precedent or previous version. Right: a pre-check report (citations, unsupported claims, defined terms, parties, dates, amounts, scope), then Approve / Request changes.

fields.name: document_version
fields.note: Pinned by hash

fields.name: destination
fields.note: client | opposing counsel | court filing | third party

fields.name: risk
fields.note: low | medium | high, set by the pre-checks

fields.name: reviewer
fields.note: A licensee with authority on the matter

fields.name: decision_note
fields.note: Required when requesting changes

fields.name: redline_set
fields.note: When the agent edited an existing document, the review item is the set of tracked changes, not the whole file

fields.name: source_highlight
fields.note: Each pre-check finding opens the cited span side by side in the viewer

actions.name: Run pre-checks
actions.note: Runs automatically when a document enters the queue

actions.name: Approve
actions.note: G8. Locks the version, records the approver, time and hash, and unblocks sending or filing.

actions.name: Request changes
actions.note: The draft returns to the drafting workspace with comments

actions.name: Approve with edits
actions.note: The lawyer's edits create a new version, and that new version is the one approved

actions.name: Delegate review
actions.note: Only to another lawyer

screens.agent: Runs the pre-checks: every factual claim cited, quotes match their sources, party names and addresses match the contact records, dates and amounts are consistent, defined terms are used consistently, no other client's names leak in, the content fits the retainer scope, and there is no privileged internal content in an external document. Sorts the queue by due date and risk.
screens.gate: G8: a named lawyer approves the exact version of each outgoing document or filing. Without that approval the system cannot email, portal-share, e-sign or file it.
edge: Pre-checks fail on an unverified authority in a court filing: Approve requires an explicit acknowledgement
The document changes after approval: the approval is void and it goes back into the queue
The reviewer is not on the matter, or is behind an ethical wall: they cannot see it
Urgent filing at the deadline: no bypass. The queue escalates to the backup lawyer instead.
screens.reg: Supervision of non-lawyers and the AI (RPC 6.1, verify). Competence (RPC 3.1). Court rules on document form (RCP, e.g. r.4) for filings (verify). LSO AI guidance: the licensee is responsible for the output.

screens.layout: Search and facets (area, document kind, clause type, jurisdiction, date). Results as cards with a preview. Detail view: the anonymized text, the clause breakdown, and usage stats (times used, last reviewed).

fields.name: kind
fields.note: full document | clause

fields.name: tags
fields.note: For example: abatement, force majeure, limited scope

fields.name: source_matter
fields.note: Visible only to people with access to that matter

fields.name: anonymized
fields.note: Client and party details removed

fields.name: status
fields.note: proposed | approved | stale | retired

fields.name: review_due
fields.note: Periodic re-review for currency of law

actions.name: Propose from matter document
actions.note: Anyone can nominate a document

actions.name: Anonymize
actions.note: Removes names, addresses, amounts and identifying facts, and shows a diff of what changed

actions.name: Admit to library
actions.note: G-D3: a lawyer confirms the anonymization and the quality

actions.name: Flag stale
actions.note: When the review date passes or a cited statute or rule changes

actions.name: Use in draft
actions.note: Opens the AI drafting workspace with this precedent selected

screens.agent: Suggests precedent candidates from approved outgoing documents that drew no changes. Anonymizes them. Splits documents into tagged clauses. Flags stale precedents. Picks the best precedents when drafting.
screens.gate: G-D3: a lawyer approves each precedent's admission, which covers both the anonymization and the legal quality.
edge: Anonymization misses an identifier: it is visible in the diff, and the lawyer must tick 'no client-identifying info remains'
A precedent from a matter that later becomes conflicted or walled: it stays in the library only in anonymized form, and the source link is hidden
The law changes: the agent flags dependent precedents and templates together
screens.reg: Confidentiality (RPC 3.3) continues after the retainer ends. Reusing client documents needs real anonymization. Precedents never cross firm cells.

screens.name: Email filing
screens.purpose: Get every matter email and its attachments into the matter file without manual forwarding.
screens.layout: Matter tab: filed threads with attachments, filed-by and confidence. Settings: connected mailboxes, matter forwarding addresses, filing rules, review queue for uncertain emails.

fields.name: mailbox
fields.note: Connected Microsoft 365 or Google account per user; shared mailboxes allowed

fields.name: rule
fields.note: by known contact address | by matter number in subject | by forward-to address | agent suggestion

fields.name: attachments
fields.note: Saved as matter documents, linked to the email

fields.name: time_entry_hint
fields.note: Suggests a time entry; billing area owns it

actions.name: Auto-file
actions.note: Only above confidence threshold

actions.name: Confirm uncertain filing
actions.note: G-D1

actions.name: Exclude address or domain
actions.note: e.g. personal emails, newsletters

screens.agent: Files emails by contact and matter number, splits a thread that spans two matters, saves attachments, and queues anything uncertain.
screens.gate: Uncertain or multi-matter emails need a human to confirm (G-D1).
edge: A contact is a party on two matters: never auto-file, ask
An email to the client cc's opposing counsel: filed, privilege flag off
Sender is on a walled matter the user is screened from: filed only to that matter, hidden from the user
Mailbox token expires: banner and admin alert, no silent gap
screens.reg: Email is part of the client file (LSO record keeping, verify).

screens.name: Client sharing and secure links
screens.purpose: Control what the client (or co-counsel) can see and download, by portal or by an expiring secure link.
screens.layout: List of shared items with who, how (portal or link), expiry, opened/downloaded marks; side panel to add a share; tab for client uploads.

fields.name: item
fields.note: Document or folder; folder share includes later files

fields.name: recipient
fields.note: Client, co-counsel or other named person

fields.name: method
fields.note: portal | secure link (no account, email code)

fields.name: expires_at
fields.note: Required for secure links; default 14 days

fields.name: upload_folder
fields.note: Client uploads land here, max size per file

fields.name: recipient_kind
fields.note: client | co-counsel | opposing. Co-counsel gets a two-way upload folder and a stop-sharing control.

fields.name: folder_rule
fields.note: Shown on screen: sharing a folder shares only items already approved under G8. New files added to a shared folder are queued for G8, never shared automatically (Clio auto-includes later files).

fields.name: co_counsel_link_days
fields.note: Expiry for emailed co-counsel links. Default 7 days (Clio uses 7).

actions.name: Share
actions.note: Outgoing documents still pass G8 if not yet reviewed

actions.name: Request documents from client
actions.note: Checklist of what is missing, e.g. ID, lease, pay stubs

actions.name: Stop sharing with co-counsel
actions.note: Revokes all links and the upload folder at once

screens.agent: Builds the request list from the matter type, chases missing uploads, and warns when a folder share would expose a privileged or internal file.
screens.gate: Lawyer approves sharing any document that has not passed G8.
edge: A file is added later to a shared folder but is marked internal: not shared, with a warning
Client forwards a secure link: second device must pass the email code
Client upload contains malware: quarantined, staff told
Co-counsel share on a matter with a wall: blocked for screened people
Co-counsel uploads a file: ingest-document files it with source = co-counsel and runs G-D1 checks before anyone on the firm side relies on it

screens.name: Deleted documents
screens.purpose: Recover deleted documents within a window, and permanently delete only when retention and holds allow.
screens.layout: Table of deleted items with who deleted, when, days left; filters by matter; restore and purge buttons.

fields.name: restore_until
fields.note: Default 30 days

fields.name: hold
fields.note: Legal hold or retention class blocks purge

actions.name: Purge now
actions.note: Lawyer; removes all versions; logged

actions.name: Auto-purge
actions.note: Agent proposes the purge list at window end (no hold, retention allows); nothing is destroyed until a lawyer approves G14

screens.agent: Purges expired items that have no hold; reports anything blocked.
screens.gate: Permanent deletion before the window ends needs a lawyer.
edge: Document deleted from a closed matter under retention: deletion refused, not trashed
Restoring into a folder that was removed: restored to matter root
Signed engagement letter deleted: refused, signed records are protected
screens.reg: File retention after closing (LSO guidance, verify).

screens.name: Document settings
screens.purpose: Firm-wide rules for documents: types, folder templates, file naming, merge fields, signing defaults and limits.
screens.layout: Sections: Types, Folder templates per practice area, Naming, Data fields catalog (with preview against a chosen matter), Signing defaults, Limits.

fields.name: doc_types
fields.note: Used for filing and reports

fields.name: folder_templates
fields.note: Practice area -> folder tree created on matter open

fields.name: naming_rule
fields.note: e.g. {date} {doc_type} {party}; agent applies on filing

fields.name: field_catalog
fields.note: Every fillable field with source (contact, matter, custom field) and preview value

fields.name: sign_defaults
fields.note: Expiry days (14), reminder days, sequential by default, identity check level

actions.name: Preview fields on a matter
actions.note: Blank means the matter is missing that data

screens.agent: Flags fields used in templates that no matter type collects, and naming collisions.
screens.gate: Folder template and signing default changes need an admin.
edge: A custom field is renamed: templates using it are listed and re-linked
Folder template changed: applies to new matters only

rows: Agreement, Title search, Closing, Correspondence, Trust

screens.name: Analyze several documents
screens.purpose: Ask one question across many matter documents (chronology, parties, obligations, inconsistencies) and keep the result.
screens.layout: Left: picked documents with page counts. Centre: question and answer with citations to page and line. Right: save as note or new document.

fields.name: documents
fields.note: Up to 50 files; size limit per set

fields.name: depth
fields.note: quick | thorough

fields.name: citations
fields.note: Each claim links to page/paragraph

fields.name: save_as
fields.note: note | new document

fields.name: mode
fields.note: answer | table

fields.name: table_columns
fields.note: Table mode: one question per column, defined by a person or proposed by the agent; templates per practice area

fields.name: table_cells
fields.note: One row per document. Each cell holds the answer and a page:line citation, or 'not applicable' / 'not found'. Clicking a cell opens the source highlight.

fields.name: document_limit
fields.note: Stated cap per table (proposed 300 documents); above it the agent asks to split the set

actions.name: Follow-up question
actions.note: Keeps context within the session; saved results keep the thread

actions.name: Send to review
actions.note: Only if the result leaves the firm (G8)

actions.name: Export table CSV
actions.note: Citations travel as a column

actions.name: Save table as template
actions.note: Saves the columns for reuse

screens.agent: Builds chronologies, party lists, obligation tables and contradictions with citations; marks anything without support.
screens.gate: none for internal notes; G8 if sent out.
edge: Scanned file with low OCR confidence: answer warns and names the pages
Selected documents include a walled one for a screened user: removed before analysis
Password-protected file: skipped and listed
Question needs law, not facts: points to the drafting workspace
Cell answer without a citation is shown as 'unsupported' and excluded from export unless a person confirms it
screens.reg: AI use with confidential info: LSO guidance on generative AI (verify).

screens.name: Document bundle builder
screens.purpose: Combine chosen documents into one paginated PDF with tabs and an index, for a court record, a brief of documents or a closing book.
screens.layout: Left: ordered list of documents with tab labels (drag to reorder). Right: live index and page preview. Footer: output options.

fields.name: page_numbers
fields.note: continuous | per tab

actions.name: Send to review
actions.note: G8 before filing or sending

screens.agent: Proposes order by date or by court rule, writes the index, checks page limits and missing pages.
screens.gate: Bundle approved (G8) before it leaves the firm.
edge: One file is not PDF: converted, conversion noted
Total size above court portal limit: offers split into volumes (verify the limit)
Source document changes after build: bundle marked stale
screens.reg: Ontario Rules of Civil Procedure format rules for records and books of documents (verify).

screens.name: Firm library and private drafts
screens.purpose: Hold firm material that belongs to no matter (policies, checklists, forms in progress) and each person's private drafts.
screens.layout: Tabs: Firm and Private. Left: folder tree. Centre: document table with status, owner and updated date. Right: details of the selected item.

fields.name: area
fields.note: firm | private

fields.name: owner
fields.note: Private items are visible only to the owner

fields.name: status
fields.note: draft | final

actions.name: Move private draft to matter
actions.note: Runs ingest-document filing checks; privilege or low-confidence items go to G-D1

actions.name: Propose as precedent
actions.note: Goes to G-D3

actions.name: Detect matter content
actions.note: Warns when a firm-library file names a client or party, and suggests moving it to the matter

screens.agent: Indexes firm items for search. Never reads another user's private drafts. Flags firm-library files that look like matter content.
screens.gate: G-D1 when a private draft moves into a matter and is uncertain or privilege-flagged; G-D3 when a file is proposed as a precedent.
edge: Owner leaves the firm: private drafts go to a lawyer the owner names, or to the firm owner, after notice; never deleted silently
Firm admin sees neither area: firm admin manages users, not content
screens.reg: Material that identifies a client belongs in the matter file for record-keeping; the firm library is for non-client material.

entities.name: AuditEvent
entities.note: stub added by spec lint: fields to be defined by the area owner

entities.name: Clause
entities.note: stub added by spec lint: fields to be defined by the area owner

entities.name: DocumentSet
entities.note: stub added by spec lint: fields to be defined by the area owner

gates.name: Engagement letter approved
gates.blocks: Sending the letter or fee agreement for signature, and therefore the trust retainer request and matter opening

gates.name: Outgoing document approved
gates.blocks: Emailing, portal-sharing, e-signing or filing any document outside the firm

gates.name: Uncertain filing / privilege confirmed
gates.approver: clerk or lawyer (lawyer for privilege flags)
gates.blocks: Low-confidence or privilege-flagged documents stay in the filing queue, outside search and agent context, and cannot be shared

gates.name: Template version published
gates.blocks: Using that template version in assembly or engagement letters

gates.name: Precedent admitted
gates.blocks: The precedent being used by the agent or shown to other matters

agent_jobs.name: ingest-document
agent_jobs.trigger: event: upload, email-in, portal upload, scan
agent_jobs.does: OCR, line map, classify, name, file, dedupe, privilege flag, extract dates, parties and amounts
agent_jobs.output: A filed document, or a filing-queue item for G-D1. Extracted deadlines go to G7.

agent_jobs.name: draft-engagement-letter
agent_jobs.trigger: event: conflict cleared (G2) and lead accepted (G1)
agent_jobs.does: Picks the template, fills scope, fees and retainer, runs the compliance checklist
agent_jobs.output: A draft engagement letter for G5

agent_jobs.name: signature-chaser
agent_jobs.does: Sends reminders, detects bounces and expiry, files completed packages, verifies the hash
agent_jobs.output: A filed signed copy and an 'engagement signed' event for the trust retainer request

agent_jobs.name: draft-with-citations
agent_jobs.trigger: event: user instruction or task from the matter plan
agent_jobs.does: Retrieves sources and precedents, drafts, cites each claim page:line, lists unsupported claims and authorities to verify

agent_jobs.name: precheck-outgoing
agent_jobs.trigger: event: document enters the review queue
agent_jobs.does: Checks citations, quotes, names, dates, amounts, scope, cross-client leakage and privileged content
agent_jobs.output: A pre-check report and risk level for G8

agent_jobs.name: citation-staleness
agent_jobs.trigger: event: new version of a cited document
agent_jobs.does: Re-matches the quotes against the new version

agent_jobs.name: template-and-precedent-currency
agent_jobs.trigger: schedule: weekly, plus event on a known rule or form change
agent_jobs.does: Flags templates and precedents past their review date or tied to changed law or forms
agent_jobs.output: Change requests for G-D2 and stale flags for G-D3

agent_jobs.name: precedent-candidates
agent_jobs.does: Finds approved outgoing documents with no changes requested, anonymizes them and splits them into clauses

agent_jobs.name: email-filer
agent_jobs.trigger: event: email arrives in connected mailbox
agent_jobs.does: Matches to matter, files thread and attachments
agent_jobs.output: Filed email or G-D1 review item

agent_jobs.name: trash-purger
agent_jobs.does: Purges trashed documents past window with no hold

agent_jobs.name: court-form-currency
agent_jobs.does: Fetches official Ontario court form pages, compares version dates and checksums, flags firm templates built on old versions
agent_jobs.output: Flag on template-library; republish under G-D2

agent_jobs.name: assembly-on-stage
agent_jobs.trigger: event: matter opened or stage changed
agent_jobs.does: Generates the configured template set into the target folder after resolving case facts
agent_jobs.output: Draft documents for G8; fact conflicts block and notify

agent_jobs.name: tracked-revision
agent_jobs.trigger: event: revise request on an existing document
agent_jobs.does: Produces tracked changes, each with a reason and citation, instead of a rewritten file

open_questions: E-sign: build our own signing flow (full control, data in Canada) or integrate a Canadian-hosted provider? This spec assumes our own.
Which document formats are authoritative for citations: always freeze a PDF rendering of each version, including Word drafts?
Should a Word round-trip (lawyer edits in Word desktop) be supported in v1, or only in-browser editing?
OCR and embeddings: must run inside the firm's Canadian cell. Is a self-hosted OCR engine acceptable on quality?
Is a clerk allowed to clear G-D1 for privilege flags, or must it always be a lawyer?
French-language templates and signing page in v1?
Do we keep a separate approval for portal-sharing an internal document, or fold it into G8?
Retention periods per document class: should we encode the LSO guidance defaults, or have each firm set them?
Sync with external stores (OneDrive, Google Drive) in v1, or our store only?
Do we offer a Word / Outlook add-in in v1, or rely on mailbox connection and web editing?
Default secure-link expiry 14 days: right for the firm?
Saved document views and per-user columns, with a natural-language filter that compiles to a saved view? (could)
Extract Word comments and tracked changes on ingest into a read-only 'From file' block? (could)
Make 'Create PDF' a first-class document action linked to the source version hash? (could)
Bundle-builder: add matter-number footer and cover fields (title, code, date)? (could)
Template status needs-review | in-progress | ready before G-D2, with each proposed field citing its source text? (could)
Compare any two documents (not only versions) with a cited topic table? (could)
Machine translation EN<->FR, marked unverified until a person approves? (could)
Document row action 'Add time', with time proposed from edit sessions (coordinate with time area)? (could)
Minimum desktop path: 'Open in Word' using the document lock as check-out? (could)
Mobile-web scan to PDF feeding ingest-document? (could)
Signature rule format 'show field X when checkbox Y checked' spelled out? (could)
Agent fills Ontario court forms field by field with a cited source; partner or build a short list first? (could)
Tabular review cap: is 300 documents per table the right stated limit?
